Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of the signals we captured so everyone is aligned and we can scope the PoC: 

- Primary user flow: multi-turn customer support assistant that streams partial answers while ingesting a mix of short-form metadata (customer id, account data ~100 tokens) and long-form context (previous chat transcript + product docs up to ~12k tokens).
- Latency target: p50 <= 220ms for short queries; for streaming responses p95 target is 700ms for first chunk (they still want snappy first-token behaviour).
- Throughput / concurrency: expected concurrent sessions during peak ~120-180; background embedding/async rerank jobs ~10 qps.
- Input/output ceilings: typical input ~2k tokens, edge cases up to ~12k tokens; output averages 300–600 tokens, occasional 2k token summaries.
- Reliability/hedges: want graceful degrade to a smaller context model if the long-window request would violate latency SLOs; also interested in KV/prefix caching for recurring customers.

Ask: please share a small set (3–5) of representative prompt+context examples and a sample traffic profile (QPS spikes, payload size distribution). That will let us map model variants and batching vs streaming tradeoffs for the PoC.

I've attached a simple mutual action plan and a one-page PoC checklist to make timelines explicit. Proposed next steps:
1) You share sample prompts + test dataset by EOD Friday (2027-05-07).
2) Internal sizing: Aditya will produce a short perf estimate and a suggested PoC config (models, batch sizes, streaming window strategy) by Monday.
3) Ops call: schedule a 45m technical handoff next week to lock in required logs, KMS, and IP allowlisting.

Monica — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 12k token window is only for chat history + attached docs on rare escalations (estimated <2% of sessions). For most sessions we expect 1–4k combined.
- Streaming is critical for the first answer pass — customers get frustrated if there is a long pause before any text appears. Prefer a model that can stream partial completions within ~400–500ms in practice.
- We expect peak concurrency to be ~150 across regions for Q3 pilot, with most traffic concentrated in US-east.
- Security: we will need a SOC2 report and a short note on how token-level logs can be sampled (we can’t send full transcripts externally).

Looping in a few technical notes based on the prompt samples Samira shared and the targets discussed. High level: we can meet the stated SLOs but there are tradeoffs to document and a concrete PoC will be required to validate production behavior.

Key considerations and recommended initial config: 
- Model variants: serve a streaming-optimized quantized model for the day-to-day flows (gptx-stream-q4) and fall back to a higher-capacity non-streaming variant for long-window summarization jobs (gptx-large-fp16). The runtime supports automatic routing/fallbacks.
- First-token latency vs throughput: streaming first-token latency is sensitive to per-request batching. For p50 <= 220ms we should set max batch delay to ~6ms and cap concurrency per GPU lane (continuous batching enables low-latency small batches). If BrightLayer wants to push concurrency beyond 200, we’ll need additional reserved lanes or Dedicated capacity to avoid increased p95s.
- Context windows: for 8–12k token requests, expect per-token processing time to increase nonlinearly (self-attention costs). For long-window sessions we recommend offloading static docs to a document store + rerank/embed approach and only include top-k relevant chunks in the prompt to stay within latency targets.
- KV/prefix caching: high value for repeat customers — reduces token work by ~20–40% for sessions with repeated context.
- Telemetry & logs: we can provide sampled token-level traces and request/response timing. SOC2 report is in our compliance pack; I’ll attach our quick perf sketch.

Attachments: [Attachment: internal_perf_estimate.csv (csv, 12KB)]

Proposed PoC acceptance criteria (short):
- Demonstrated p50 <= 250ms for 90% of short queries on the PoC workload.
- Streaming first-chunk latency < 600ms for median cases.
- End-to-end 99th percentile for long-window summaries completes within agreed fallback SLA (to be negotiated).

If that looks good, I’ll build a short test harness and an initial config for the ops call.

— Aditya Rao
